title: Google - LLM Hallucination Detection Challenge
prompt: Identify when a large language model is 'hallucinating' or providing factually incorrect information in long-form responses. Data: LLM-generated answers paired with reference documents and human truth-labels. Goal: Predict the probability that a specific claim within a response is unsupported. Challenge: Distinguishing between stylistic variations and actual factual contradictions.
solution_summary: Cross-encoder approach using DeBERTa-v4-XXL. The winning solution implemented a 'NLI-inspired' (Natural Language Inference) pipeline where claims were atomized into individual propositions and compared against retrieved context snippets. They utilized a custom 'Contextual-Attention' head that weighted tokens based on their presence in the reference grounding text.

title: RSNA 2026 - Pancreatic Cancer Detection
prompt: Detect and segment early-stage pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma in contrast-enhanced CT scans. Data: Volumetric CT images with pixel-level masks of tumors and surrounding organs. Goal: Predict 3D segmentation masks. Challenge: Pancreatic tumors are often isodense with the surrounding tissue, making boundaries extremely difficult to visualize.
solution_summary: Hierarchical 3D Swin-UNet ensemble. 1st place utilized a coarse-to-fine strategy: a first-stage 3D model localized the pancreas, followed by a high-resolution Swin-Transformer-based UNet focused only on the pancreatic ROI. They implemented a custom 'Boundary-Refinement' loss that penalized the model for missing the subtle 'infiltrative' edges of the tumor.

title: Google Earth Engine - Wildfire Spread Prediction
evaluation_metric: Intersection over Union (IoU) on Next-Day Spread
prompt: Predict the expansion of active wildfires over the next 24 hours using satellite and weather data. Data: Daily fire perimeters, NDVI vegetation maps, fuel moisture, and hourly wind vectors. Goal: Predict a binary mask of the area likely to burn. Challenge: Modeling the stochastic nature of 'spotting' where embers jump ahead of the main fire front.
solution_summary: Vision Transformer with ConvLSTM for temporal modeling. The winning entry used a ViT-L/14 backbone to encode the landscape and a ConvLSTM to capture the fire's movement history. They integrated a 'Wind-Flow-Attention' mechanism that biased the prediction towards the downwind direction based on GFS weather forecasts.
key_techniques: NDVI and Fuel Moisture feature fusion

title: AI Mathematical Olympiad - Progress Prize 3
prompt: Solve advanced competition-level mathematics problems from the IMO shortlist using AI agents. Data: Textual math problems requiring formal proofs or integer answers. Goal: Provide the correct solution. Challenge: Problems require deep multi-step reasoning and the creation of novel lemmas that aren't present in common training corpora.
solution_summary: Lean-4 formal verification with LLM-guided search. 1st place utilized an LLM (Gemini 3 Ultra) to translate problems into Lean-4 code. An 'Agentic Search' loop attempted to find a formal proof, using the Lean compiler to provide feedback on logical errors. They implemented 'Backtracking' where the model would restart the proof if the current path became a logical dead-end.

title: Sorghum-100 Cultivar Identification
prompt: Identify different cultivars of sorghum plants from ground-level photos. Data: Thousands of images of sorghum in fields across 100 cultivars. Goal: Predict the specific cultivar. Challenge: Different cultivars look extremely similar, and images include varied lighting, soil types, and plant growth stages.
solution_summary: Ensemble of ConvNeXt and Vision Transformers with Label Smoothing. 1st place utilized an ensemble of ConvNeXt-Base and ViT-S/16. They applied 'Random Erasing' and 'MixUp' to handle the noisy background of the fields. A key insight was using 'Metadata-informed fine-tuning' where the model was first trained to predict the growth stage as an auxiliary task.

title: Bridgestone - Tire Wear and Life Prediction
prompt: Predict the remaining useful life (RUL) of tires based on vehicle sensor data. Data: Time-series of tire pressure, temperature, vehicle speed, and road roughness. Goal: Predict kilometers remaining before failure. Challenge: Tire wear is highly non-linear and depends on individual driving styles and varied environmental conditions.
solution_summary: Deep Residual LSTM with physics-informed features. 1st place utilized an ensemble of Bi-LSTMs and LightGBM. They engineered 'Cumulative-Stress' features based on a physics-based tire-degradation model. They implemented 'Style-Normalization' to account for aggressive vs. gentle drivers, significantly improving the stability of the RUL estimates.
key_techniques: Rolling window standard deviation of pressure

title: Google Earth Engine - Deforestation Detection 2026
prompt: Identify areas of illegal deforestation and forest degradation in near-real-time using satellite imagery. Data: Sentinel-2 and Landsat-9 time-series images. Goal: Predict a binary change mask indicating new clearing activity. Challenge: Differentiating between seasonal leaf-off periods and actual logging/burning activity.
solution_summary: Spatio-temporal U-Net with attention-gated Skip Connections. The 1st place solution used a 3D-UNet that processed a 6-month stack of satellite images. They implemented 'Attention Gates' that focused on sudden changes in the NDVI index while ignoring slow seasonal shifts. They utilized 'Synthetic Aperture Radar' (SAR) data to detect clearing through cloud cover.

title: LLM Efficiency - Code Generation Challenge
prompt: Optimize a coding LLM to provide the most accurate Python solutions with the least energy consumption. Data: HumanEval and MBPP benchmarks. Goal: Maximize Pass@1 while minimizing inference time and power. Challenge: Reducing model size via quantization without losing the complex reasoning needed for coding.
solution_summary: Weight-Pruned and Quantized Llama-3-70B. 1st place utilized 'SparseGPT' to prune 50% of the model weights followed by 3-bit AWQ (Activation-aware Weight Quantization). They implemented a 'Speculative Decoding' pipeline where a tiny 100M-parameter model drafted tokens for the large model to verify, increasing throughput by 3x on a single A100 GPU.

title: Ariel Data Challenge 2025 - Exoplanet Atmospheres
prompt: Extract exoplanet atmospheric transmission spectra from noisy telescope time-series data. Data: Focal plane images over the duration of a planetary transit. Goal: Predict the relative absorption across 300 wavelengths. Challenge: Separating the tiny planet signal (parts per million) from the dominant star brightness and spacecraft noise.
solution_summary: Pixel-level denoising and Deep Regression ensemble. 1st place used a 2D-CNN to remove 'hot pixels' and cosmic ray artifacts from the raw images. They then aggregated the flux into light-curves and used a Transformer model to predict the spectra. A key insight was using 'Synthetic Transit Injection' to triple the training data with known signals.

title: Google Landmark Recognition 2026 - Multimodal
prompt: Recognize world landmarks using both photos and associated metadata/descriptions. Data: 2M images and short textual descriptions (e.g., 'altar in Gothic cathedral'). Goal: Predict landmark ID. Challenge: Many landmarks have identical architectural styles; textual context is needed to distinguish between similar cathedrals or bridges.
solution_summary: Vision-Language Model (VLM) with ArcFace fusion. 1st place utilized a CLIP-style architecture (ViT-H/14) that jointly encoded image and text. They implemented 'Cross-Modal ArcFace' which aligned the image and text embeddings into a single class-discriminative space. They utilized 'Retrieval-Augmented Classification' to verify predictions against a curated landmark knowledge base.

title: Binance - Crypto Market Making Optimization
prompt: Develop a market-making agent that provides liquidity to high-volatility crypto markets. Data: L2 Order Book (DOM) and trade-by-trade logs for BTC/ETH. Goal: Minimize 'inventory risk' while maximizing 'spread capture'. Challenge: High-frequency 'toxic flow' where informed traders pick off stale quotes.
solution_summary: Deep Reinforcement Learning with PPO and LSTM. 1st place utilized 'Proximal Policy Optimization' (PPO) to control quote placement. They used an LSTM to encode the recent order-book history and predicted 'Order Flow Toxicity' as an auxiliary signal. They implemented 'Reward Shaping' that penalized the agent for holding large imbalanced positions.

title: Amazon - Robotic Arm Pose Estimation
prompt: Predict the joint angles of a robotic arm from a single RGB camera view to improve pick-and-place accuracy. Data: 2D images and corresponding 3D ground-truth angles for a 7-DOF arm. Goal: Predict 7 continuous angles. Challenge: Self-occlusion where parts of the arm hide other joints from the camera.
solution_summary: 3D-Pose estimation via Heatmap Regression and GNN. 1st place utilized a HRNet to predict 2D keypoints for each joint, followed by a Graph Neural Network (GNN) that mapped the 2D keypoints to 3D joint angles using the known kinematic chain constraints. They used 'Synthetic-to-Real' domain adaptation to leverage massive CAD-rendered data.

title: UBC - Whole Slide Lung Cancer Subtyping
prompt: Classify lung cancer subtypes (Adenocarcinoma vs Squamous Cell) from multi-gigapixel histopathology slides. Data: Whole Slide Images (WSI) with varied magnification. Goal: Predict subtype. Challenge: Identifying tiny malignant regions within a massive image containing healthy tissue and inflammation.
solution_summary: Multiple Instance Learning (MIL) with Vision Transformer embeddings. 1st place extracted tiles at 20x magnification and encoded them using a Phikon-foundation model. They utilized a 'Gated-Attention MIL' aggregator that learned to ignore non-tumor tiles. They implemented a 'Feature-Clustering' step to identify and exclude areas with poor staining or artifacts.

title: GridAware - Energy Grid Stability Prediction 2026
prompt: Predict power grid instability and potential blackouts caused by renewable energy fluctuations. Data: High-frequency phasor measurement unit (PMU) data (voltage, frequency, phase angle). Goal: Predict 'Instability' events 5 minutes in advance. Challenge: Detecting the subtle 'oscillatory' patterns that precede a major grid failure.
solution_summary: Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) with Fourier features. 1st place used a TCN to process the PMU time-series. They implemented a 'Fourier-Attention' layer that specifically looked for sub-synchronous oscillations in the frequency domain. They used a 'Contrastive Loss' to separate normal grid noise from pre-failure signatures.

title: DJI - Autonomous Drone Navigation Challenge 2026
prompt: Train a drone to navigate a complex indoor obstacle course using only on-board camera and IMU. Data: Stereo video feeds and accelerometer/gyroscope logs in a simulated environment. Goal: Reach the finish line. Challenge: Real-time obstacle avoidance with limited compute and handling motion blur during high-speed maneuvers.
solution_summary: Model-Free Reinforcement Learning with SAC and Vision-Backbone. 1st place utilized 'Soft Actor-Critic' (SAC) with a MobileNet-v3 vision encoder. They implemented 'Domain Randomization' (varying lighting/textures) to ensure the agent generalized from simulation to reality. They used a 'Depth-Prediction' auxiliary task to help the drone estimate obstacle distances.

title: US Census Bureau - Household Demographics Prediction
prompt: Predict household income categories and family structures from anonymized census data. Data: Hundreds of categorical features (education, occupation, age, housing). Goal: Predict multi-class demographic status. Challenge: Handling significant missing data and the complex interactions between geographic and socio-economic variables.
solution_summary: Ensemble of TabNet and Gradient Boosting with Geo-Aggregation. 1st place utilized 'TabNet', a deep learning model for tabular data with internal attention, and LightGBM. They implemented 'Geo-Spatial Aggregation' where they created features based on the average income and education of the surrounding census tract. They used 'Iterative Imputation' for missing markers.

title: DESI - Identifying Anomalous Galaxies
prompt: Identify rare and anomalous astronomical objects (e.g., merging galaxies, quasars) in the DESI Legacy Survey. Data: Multi-band sky images and spectroscopic features. Goal: Predict 'Anomalous' vs 'Normal' galaxy. Challenge: The 'Anomalous' class is extremely rare (0.01%) and varies greatly in visual appearance.
solution_summary: Unsupervised Anomaly Detection using Contrastive Learning. 1st place utilized a 'Self-Supervised' pre-training on 2M normal galaxies using the SimCLR framework. They then used a 'Density-based' score in the latent space to identify outliers. They fine-tuned on a small set of 1,000 manually labeled anomalies using a 'One-class SVM' head.

title: Booking.com Multi-Destination Prediction
prompt: Predict the final destination city of a multi-city trip based on the previous cities visited. Data: Millions of anonymized user booking sequences. Goal: Predict the top 4 candidate cities. Challenge: The 'trip intent' shifts throughout the journey; the model must capture long-term travel patterns from short sequences.
solution_summary: Sequence modeling with Bi-GRU and Item-Collaborative Filtering. 1st place utilized a Bidirectional GRU to encode the trip history and combined it with a 'Transition Matrix' that measured the probability of moving from city A to B globally. They used 'Target Encoding' for the specific city IDs and applied a 'Popularity-Bias' correction for major hubs like Paris or London.
key_techniques: Target encoding for City and Country IDs

title: NeurIPS 2025 - Protein Folding Stability Prediction
prompt: Predict the thermodynamic stability of protein variants created by single-point mutations. Data: Protein sequences and 3D crystal structures (PDB). Goal: Predict the change in free energy (DeltaDelta G). Challenge: Modeling the delicate physical interactions at the mutation site while generalizing to unseen protein folds.
solution_summary: Geometric Deep Learning with ProteinMPNN. The winning entry utilized a 'Geometric Transformer' that operated on the 3D coordinates of the alpha-carbon atoms. They implemented a 'Local-Environment' encoder that captured the hydrogen-bonding and hydrophobic interactions around the mutation site. They used 'Pre-training' on the AlphaFold-2 database.

title: Google AI - Sentiment for Low-Resource Languages
prompt: Perform sentiment analysis on social media posts in low-resource languages (e.g., Yoruba, Quechua, Khmer). Data: 50k labeled posts in 20 languages. Goal: Predict Positive, Negative, or Neutral sentiment. Challenge: Minimal pre-training data available for these languages, requiring cross-lingual transfer from English or Spanish.
solution_summary: Ensemble of XLM-RoBERTa-Large and adapter-based fine-tuning. 1st place utilized 'Language Adapters'—small modular layers inserted into the XLM-R backbone for each language. They implemented 'Intermediate-Task' fine-tuning on a larger multilingual toxic-comment dataset before training on the target sentiment task. They utilized 'Back-Translation' to augment the training sets.

title: Predicting Crypto Market Microstructure 2025
prompt: Predict short-term price movements and order book imbalance in cryptocurrency markets. Data: Tick-by-tick order book data at 1ms resolution. Goal: Predict price change over the next 10 seconds. Challenge: Capturing the extremely high-velocity signals and identifying 'phantom' orders meant to manipulate the market.
solution_summary: 1D-CNN and LSTM ensemble with 'Order Flow' features. 1st place used a 1D-CNN to extract features from the L3 message stream (adds/cancels) and an LSTM to model the temporal evolution of the mid-price. They engineered 'Order Flow Imbalance' (OFI) features at multiple depths of the book and used 'Target Denoising' via a Kalman Filter.

title: Sea Turtle Face Detection and Re-Identification
prompt: Identify individual sea turtles from photos of their facial scales (which are unique like fingerprints). Data: 10k images of sea turtles with individual IDs. Goal: Match new photos to a known database. Challenge: Photos are taken underwater with varied clarity, bubbles, and perspective distortion.
solution_summary: Metric Learning with ArcFace and Scale-Attention. 1st place utilized an ensemble of ConvNeXt-Large and EfficientNet-v2. They implemented a 'Scale-Attention' module that helped the model focus specifically on the geometric pattern of the turtle's facial scales. They used 'Geometric Warping' to normalize the turtle's head pose before feature extraction.

title: Santa 2025 - The Snowplow Routing Problem
prompt: Coordinate a fleet of snowplows to clear all streets in a virtual city with minimum total time. Data: X, Y coordinates and street lengths for 100k nodes. Goal: Find optimal paths for 10 snowplows. Challenge: Streets must be cleared in a specific order based on 'priority' levels, and plows must return to the depot for fuel.
solution_summary: Modified LKH-3 with Priority Constraints and Parallel Search. 1st place utilized the LKH-3 solver, adapted for 'Multi-Depot VRP' with priority windows. They implemented a 'Cluster-then-Route' approach where they first partitioned the city into 10 balanced zones using K-Means++ and then optimized each plow's path independently using 2-opt and 3-opt moves.

title: CERN - TrackML Particle Reconstruction 2.0
prompt: Reconstruct the paths of subatomic particles from silicon detector 'hits' in the Large Hadron Collider. Data: 3D coordinates (x, y, z) of millions of hits per event. Goal: Assign each hit to the correct particle 'track'. Challenge: Hits from thousands of particles are overlapping, requiring the identification of precise helical trajectories.
solution_summary: Graph Neural Network (GNN) with Edge-Classification. 1st place utilized an Interaction Network (GNN) to predict whether two hits were produced by the same particle (edge classification). They implemented a 'Helix-Guided-Attention' layer that utilized the known physics of particle motion in a magnetic field. They used 'DBSCAN' on the predicted edge-probabilities to cluster hits into tracks.

title: Visa - Transaction Fraud Detection with GNNs
prompt: Identify fraudulent credit card transactions by modeling the relationships between merchants, users, and banks. Data: 50M transactions with time, amount, and ID metadata. Goal: Predict binary fraud status. Challenge: Fraudsters use 'complex multi-hop' networks to hide money laundering, which traditional models miss.
solution_summary: Heterogeneous Graph Neural Network (HGNN) with Temporal Edge-Attention. 1st place utilized a GraphSAGE architecture adapted for multiple node types. They implemented a 'Temporal Edge-Attention' layer that prioritized recent transactions between nodes. They used 'Neighbor-Sampling' to train on the massive graph and utilized an ensemble of HGNN and CatBoost.
key_techniques: Handling imbalanced fraud labels via weighting

title: Amazon - Multilingual E-commerce Product Classification
prompt: Classify millions of products into a 5,000-class taxonomy across 30 languages. Data: Product titles and descriptions in English, Hindi, Arabic, etc. Goal: Predict the correct category. Challenge: Managing 'taxonomy drift' where the same item is classified differently across cultures and handling high-cardinality labels.
solution_summary: Dual-Encoder with Cross-Lingual Projection. 1st place utilized a XLM-RoBERTa-Large backbone. They implemented a 'Taxonomy-Embedding' head where each category was represented as a vector in the same latent space as the product descriptions. They used 'Cross-Lingual Pseudo-labeling' to use English labels to train models for low-resource languages.

title: Meta - GenAI Video and Deepfake Detection
prompt: Detect whether a video is real or generated/manipulated by AI (Deepfakes, Sora-generated). Data: 100k videos with varied quality and compression. Goal: Predict the probability of being AI-generated. Challenge: New generative models (like Veo or Sora) produce fewer artifacts, making them nearly indistinguishable from real footage.
solution_summary: Spatio-Temporal Transformer with 3D-CNN features. 1st place utilized an ensemble of Video-Swin-Transformer and EfficientNet-v2. They implemented a 'Temporal-Artifact' head that looked for inconsistency in the movement of eyelids and lips over 30-frame sequences. They utilized 'Adversarial Training' where the model was trained against a dynamically updated generator.

title: NASA - Exoplanet Atmosphere Signature Extraction
prompt: Identify the chemical signatures of water, methane, and oxygen in the atmospheres of distant exoplanets. Data: Hyperspectral time-series data from the James Webb Space Telescope. Goal: Predict the molecular concentration. Challenge: Separating the planet's atmospheric signal from the star's much stronger spectral lines and noise from telescope jitters.
solution_summary: Physics-Informed Deep Regression with Spectral-Detrending. 1st place utilized a Transformer-based architecture to process the hyperspectral data. They implemented a 'Star-Subtraction' layer that used a physical model of the parent star to isolate the planet's transmission spectrum. They used 'Synthetic Data Injection' to train on rare atmospheric compositions.

title: Anthropic - LLM Human Alignment Preference
prompt: Develop a reward model that accurately predicts human preferences for LLM responses based on 'Helpfulness' and 'Harmlessness'. Data: Prompt-response pairs with binary 'A vs B' human labels. Goal: Predict which response is better. Challenge: Humans often disagree on subtle nuances, requiring a model that can handle 'noisy' labels and diverse ethical viewpoints.
solution_summary: Bradley-Terry Reward Model with Multi-Head Preference. 1st place utilized a Llama-3-70B model as a reward model backbone. They implemented 'Multi-Head Preference' where separate heads were trained for helpfulness and harmlessness. They utilized 'Active Learning' to identify the most ambiguous samples for the model and focused training on those edge cases.

title: Predicting Quantum Chemical Properties 2025
prompt: Predict the scalar coupling constants between atoms in a molecule using quantum mechanics features. Data: 3D coordinates of atoms and bonding types. Goal: Predict the magnetic interaction strength. Challenge: Capturing the long-range electronic effects that influence coupling across several bonds without expensive DFT calculations.
solution_summary: SchNet with Tensor-Field Networks. The winning solution utilized a 'SchNet' architecture, which uses continuous-filter convolutions to model 3D molecular structures. They implemented 'Tensor-Field' layers that were equivariant to 3D rotation and translation. A key insight was using 'Multi-path Message Passing' to model both through-bond and through-space interactions.

title: Google Earth Engine - Regional Crop Yield Forecast
prompt: Forecast the yield of major food crops (rice, corn, wheat) 3 months before harvest. Data: Multi-spectral satellite time-series and local soil moisture sensors. Goal: Predict metric tons per hectare. Challenge: Modeling the impact of 'short-duration' weather shocks like heatwaves during the flowering stage which drastically reduce yield.
solution_summary: Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) with Attention-based Weather Fusion. 1st place utilized a TCN to encode the 12-month vegetation cycle. They implemented a 'Weather-Impact Attention' layer that gave higher weights to weather anomalies occurring during critical growth stages. They used 'Pseudo-labeling' from previous high-yield years to stabilize the model.

title: RSNA 2025 - Scoliosis Cobb Angle Measurement
prompt: Automatically measure the Cobb angle (spine curvature) in spinal X-rays to monitor scoliosis. Data: Frontal and lateral spine X-rays with annotated vertebrae. Goal: Predict the curvature angle in degrees. Challenge: Precisely identifying the 'end vertebrae' (the most tilted ones) which determines the angle, a task prone to human-rater variability.
solution_summary: 2-stage Detection and Geometric Regression. 1st place used a YOLOv8-X model to detect and segment individual vertebrae. The output coordinates were fed into a 'Geometric-Differentiable' layer that calculated the angle based on the most extreme tilts. They utilized 'Consistency-Regularization' to ensure that frontal and lateral predictions resulted in a coherent 3D spine model.

title: Google - LLM Fine-tuning for Code Generation
prompt: Fine-tune a base LLM to produce bug-free and efficient Python code for complex programming tasks. Data: 1M Python coding problems with unit tests. Goal: Achieve the highest Pass@1 score. Challenge: Preventing the model from producing 'nearly correct' but logically flawed code that fails edge-case tests.
solution_summary: Instruction-tuning with Reinforcement Learning from Unit Tests (RLUT). 1st place utilized 'Proximal Policy Optimization' (PPO) where the reward was directly tied to the unit-test pass rate. They implemented 'Execution-Feedback' loops during training, where the model could see its own error messages and attempt to correct the code.

title: Google Earth Engine - Urban Change Detection 2026
prompt: Detect new building construction and road expansion in global cities using high-resolution satellite imagery. Data: Maxar satellite images at 30cm resolution. Goal: Predict a binary mask for new infrastructure. Challenge: Differentiating between temporary construction (e.g., cranes, shadows) and actual finished buildings.
solution_summary: Spatio-Temporal Attention U-Net. 1st place utilized a HRNet-based UNet that processed image pairs (Before and After). They implemented a 'Change-Aware Attention' layer that focused on spectral differences indicative of concrete and asphalt. They used 'Shadow-Inference' to estimate the 3D height of new buildings to verify they weren't just ground-level artifacts.

title: Home Credit - Credit Scoring for Underbanked Populations
prompt: Predict creditworthiness for individuals with no traditional credit history using alternative data sources. Data: Mobile phone usage, utility payments, and shopping patterns. Goal: Predict binary default status. Challenge: The data is highly heterogeneous and noisy, with significant missing values across different sources.
solution_summary: Stacked ensemble of TabNet and CatBoost with source-specific embeddings. 1st place utilized a 'Source-Aware Transformer' that learned separate embeddings for mobile data vs. utility data. They implemented 'Denoising Autoencoders' to fill missing values and used CatBoost to capture non-linear interactions in the socio-economic features.

title: Halite IV - Autonomous Ship Competition
prompt: Develop an AI agent to control a fleet of ships to collect 'halite' (resources) in a space-themed game. Data: Game state updates every turn. Goal: Out-collect other agents over 400 turns. Challenge: Strategic planning, avoiding collisions, and managing the cost of 'spawning' new ships versus the resource gain.
solution_summary: Hybrid Reinforcement Learning and Rule-based logic. The 1st place solution used 'Proximal Policy Optimization' (PPO) to train the low-level movement of individual ships. They combined this with a high-level 'Rule-based' conductor that managed fleet-wide logistics (e.g., when to return to base). They used 'Self-play' against thousands of previous agent versions.

title: WiDS Datathon 2024 - Equity in Healthcare
prompt: Identify disparities in cancer diagnosis and treatment based on socio-economic and environmental factors. Data: Patient medical records and neighborhood demographic data (pollution, income, transit). Goal: Predict the likelihood of late-stage diagnosis. Challenge: Accounting for 'hidden' biases in clinical data while maintaining high predictive accuracy.
solution_summary: Ensemble of LightGBM and XGBoost with Bias-Aware feature selection. 1st place utilized 'Fairness-Regularization' to ensure the model's predictions were consistent across different racial and economic subgroups. They implemented 'Environmental-Context' features by matching patient zip codes to EPA air-quality indices and census-tract income levels.

title: SaaS - Predicting Enterprise User Churn
prompt: Predict which enterprise customers are likely to cancel their software subscription. Data: Feature usage logs, customer support tickets, and billing history. Goal: Predict binary churn status. Challenge: Identifying 'silent churn' where usage slowly declines over months before a final cancellation.
solution_summary: Time-series aggregation with CatBoost. 1st place utilized a multi-window approach, creating features that measured the 'velocity' of feature usage change (e.g., usage at T minus usage at T-30 days). They implemented 'Target Encoding' for the specific software modules and used 'Support-Ticket Sentiment' as a secondary feature using a small BERT model.

title: NASA - Airport Pushback Characterization
prompt: Predict the exact 'pushback' time for aircraft at busy airports to optimize runway scheduling. Data: Flight schedules, METAR weather data, and real-time airport ground traffic. Goal: Predict minutes from schedule to actual move. Challenge: Managing the 'ripple effect' where one delayed flight affects all subsequent gate assignments.
solution_summary: Ensemble of LightGBM and LSTM with 'Airport-State' encoding. 1st place utilized a LightGBM model to capture tabular features like flight type and an LSTM to model the current queue of aircraft at the airport. They implemented a 'Congestion-Index' feature that measured the number of active ground moves per hour, which was the single most predictive signal.

title: Google Earth Engine - Global Wildfire Severity 2026
evaluation_metric: Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) on Burn Severity
prompt: Predict the burn severity of active wildfires to prioritize disaster response resources. Data: Sentinel-2 post-fire imagery and multi-temporal moisture levels. Goal: Predict the 'Difference Normalized Burn Ratio' (dNBR). Challenge: Differentiating between high-severity fire and natural forest gaps in dense canopy areas.
solution_summary: Multi-modal U-Net with Residual-Attention. 1st place utilized a U-Net architecture that fused RGB, NIR, and SWIR (Short-Wave Infrared) bands. They implemented a 'Residual-Attention' block that helped the model focus on the drastic spectral changes between pre-fire and post-fire observations. They used 'Pseudo-labeling' from high-resolution drone surveys to refine the masks.

title: Google Landmark Recognition 2025 - Global Search
prompt: Identify world landmarks in images across 100,000+ classes from around the globe. Data: 3M images with high label noise and varied viewing angles. Goal: Predict landmark ID. Challenge: Extreme 'fine-grained' architectural differences between similar-style buildings across different cities.
solution_summary: Sub-center ArcFace with Global and Local Descriptors. 1st place utilized an ensemble of ConvNeXt-XL and DeiT-Large models. They implemented 'Sub-center ArcFace' to handle intra-class visual diversity (e.g., inside vs outside of a museum) and utilized 'Local Feature Re-ranking' using DELF to confirm the most ambiguous predictions.

title: Google ASL Fingerspelling 2024
prompt: Translate fingerspelled American Sign Language from mobile video frames into text. Data: Hand-landmark sequences (x, y, z) from MediaPipe. Goal: Predict the character string. Challenge: Extremely high-speed signing (>5 characters per second) where individual frames are highly blurred.
solution_summary: Squeeze-and-Excitation Transformer with CTC Loss. 1st place utilized a 12-layer Transformer encoder with 'Squeeze-and-Excitation' blocks to weight landmark importance. They implemented 'CTC Loss' (Connectionist Temporal Classification) to handle the alignment between signing frames and characters. They used 'Temporal-Drop' to make the model robust to dropped video frames.

title: Foursquare - Location Matching
prompt: Match different listings for the same business/location from multiple sources. Data: Listing names, addresses, and GPS coordinates. Goal: Predict which pairs of IDs represent the same place. Challenge: Non-standard naming (e.g., 'Starbucks' vs 'Starbucks Coffee') and noisy, approximate GPS coordinates.
solution_summary: Two-stage Retrieval and GBDT Ranking. 1st place used 'K-Nearest Neighbors' (KNN) on GPS coordinates to find the top 50 candidates for each listing. In the second stage, they used an XGBoost model to rank these candidates using string-similarity features (Levenshtein, Jaccard) and geographic distance. They used 'Cross-feature interactions' like 'Name-match AND Distance < 10m'.

title: Shopee - Price Match Guarantee
prompt: Identify duplicate product listings across different sellers based on images and titles. Data: Images, product titles, and seller info. Goal: Predict all IDs that match a given product. Challenge: Visually similar products with different packaging and titles in multiple languages.
solution_summary: Multimodal Metric Learning with ArcFace. 1st place utilized an ensemble of EfficientNet-B3 (for images) and RoBERTa-Base (for titles). They mapped both images and text into a shared 512-dimensional embedding space using ArcFace loss. They utilized 'Nearest-Neighbor' search with a specific threshold to find clusters of identical products.

title: Eedi - Mining Misconceptions in Mathematics
prompt: Identify the specific mathematical misconception a student holds based on their wrong answer to a diagnostic question. Data: Math questions, the student's incorrect choice, and a list of 2,000+ known misconceptions. Goal: Predict the correct misconception ID. Challenge: Understanding the 'logic' behind a wrong answer across varied math topics.
solution_summary: Cross-Encoder retrieval using DeBERTa-v3-Large. 1st place utilized a two-stage approach: a Bi-Encoder first retrieved the top 100 candidate misconceptions, followed by a DeBERTa-v3-Large Cross-Encoder that ranked the candidates by reasoning through the question text. They utilized 'Chain-of-Thought' augmentation during training to help the model learn the steps of wrong-answer logic.

title: Google Smartphone Decimeter Challenge 2021
prompt: Improve smartphone GPS accuracy by processing raw GNSS measurements. Data: Raw pseudorange and carrier-phase logs from smartphones. Goal: Predict latitude/longitude. Challenge: Correcting for massive multipath noise and 'cycle slips' in urban canyons.
solution_summary: EKF with Carrier-Phase smoothing and RTS Backward filtering. 1st place utilized an Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) that combined pseudorange with 'Phase-Difference' measurements. They implemented a 'Rauch-Tung-Striebel' (RTS) backward smoother to refine the entire trajectory. They used road-snapping via a Hidden Markov Model (HMM) to improve suburban driving accuracy.

title: Google Landmark Retrieval 2018
prompt: Find matching images for a query landmark image from a database of 1M+ photos. Data: Query photos and an index set. Goal: Return a ranked list of relevant images. Challenge: Handling 'distractor' images and achieving high retrieval speed while maintaining precision for rare landmarks.
solution_summary: Global descriptor retrieval with DELF re-ranking. 1st place utilized an ensemble of ResNet-101 models to extract global descriptors. They implemented 'Query Expansion' (QE) and 'Database Augmentation' (DBA) to improve the initial retrieval set. They used 'DELF' (Deep Local Features) for geometric verification of the top candidates using RANSAC.

title: Google ASL Fingerspelling 2026 - Edge Edition
prompt: Optimize ASL fingerspelling translation for low-power mobile devices. Data: Hand-landmark sequences from mobile cameras. Goal: Predict the character string. Challenge: Achieving high accuracy with a model small enough to run in real-time (<50ms latency) on an entry-level smartphone.
solution_summary: Knowledge Distillation from a Large Transformer to a Tiny SqueezeNet. 1st place utilized a 'Teacher-Student' framework where a large 24-layer Transformer taught a 4-layer MobileNet-v3 based student. They implemented 'Quantization-Aware Training' (QAT) to compress the model to 8-bit integers without losing accuracy on fast-signing sequences.

title: Google Landmark Retrieval 2022
prompt: Find matching landmark images in a massive index given a query image. Data: 1M+ images. Goal: Return matching landmarks. Challenge: Visual similarity between buildings across the globe and handling nocturnal vs diurnal photos of the same site.
solution_summary: Ensemble of Vision Transformers with Cosine Similarity search. 1st place utilized an ensemble of DeiT and ConvNeXt backbones trained with ArcFace loss. They implemented 'Style-Invariant' augmentation where they synthesized night-time versions of day-time photos to force the model to focus on geometry rather than lighting. They used 'Database Augmentation' (DBA).

title: Google Landmark Recognition 2023
prompt: Identify world landmarks in images across 100,000+ classes. Data: 4M images with high label noise. Goal: Predict landmark ID. Challenge: Extreme class cardinality and the long-tail distribution where thousands of classes have only 1-2 examples.
solution_summary: Sub-center ArcFace with Dynamic Margin Scaling. 1st place utilized an ensemble of EfficientNet-B7 and ConvNeXt-Large. They implemented 'Dynamic Margin Scaling' where the ArcFace margin was increased for rare classes to improve separation. They used 'Pseudo-labeling' to use a large pool of unlabeled travel photos from the internet.

title: Google Landmark Recognition 2024
prompt: Recognize world landmarks from a globally diverse dataset of 5M+ images. Data: High-resolution images from travel blogs and citizen science. Goal: Predict landmark ID. Challenge: Handling the visual shift between professional travel photos and low-quality mobile uploads.
solution_summary: Ensemble of Foundation Vision-Language Models. 1st place utilized a CLIP-style visual backbone fine-tuned for landmark retrieval. They implemented 'Domain-Adversarial training' where the model was forced to produce identical features for professional and mobile photos of the same site. They used 'Balanced Sampling' to handle the massive class imbalance.
